title: graphrefly-rs DeferredCtx holds a STRONG Core (Rc<RefCell<NodeInner>>): an async fn that stashes ctx.defer() and never emits (abandoned/cancelled work, a never-resolving backend) pins the node's NodeInner — and thus its fn slot (blocking the B32 unregister), its captured upstream Cores, and its dep_unsubs subscriptions — alive until the DeferredCtx drops. title: RxJS-7 time-operator complete-edge reference (context7-verified /reactivex/rxjs 7.8.2, 2026-05-30) -- pins the per-operator source-COMPLETE behavior so it is settled BEFORE implementation, NOT left to discover. outcome: Separate durable decisions from work-linked execution authorization, attempts and evidence
acceptance: A separately approved design review defines four disjoint identity and authority classes: durable semantic decisions use origin-qualified D#; owner-local work or evaluation charters use work identities; explicit human run or spend authorization uses a non-decision execution-authorization identity; attempts, incidents, receipts and evidence use immutable non-authority identities. Execution authorization must not enter the durable-decision current view or reuse the D# namespace.

One evaluation charter binds an unchanged semantic question, success criteria, frozen task or input set, evaluation and verifier revisions, total budget ceiling, stop conditions and required evidence. Repeated runs, repairs or model/provider substitutions inside those approved bounds remain attempts under the same charter and do not mint decisions or new work items.

Every provider call, live rerun or additional spend remains manual-first and requires an explicit, bounded, single-use or quantity-bounded human authorization linked to the exact owner-local work or charter, risk and capability coordinates, budget increment or ceiling, expiry and replay protection. A new authorization advances permission only; it does not claim architectural progress, alter success criteria, approve implementation or dispatch unrelated work.

A materially changed semantic contract or success criterion requires the normal durable-decision process; a materially changed objective or separately reviewable work outcome requires the normal owner-local work-admission process. Neither case may be hidden inside an execution authorization, while provider, model, attempt or budget-coordinate changes alone do not create a durable D#.

Qualification covers replayed, expired, stale, over-budget, wrong-charter, wrong-provider or model, wrong-task-set and post-stop authorization; repeated-failure handling must compress attempted routes into exact evidence refs, expose the current blocker and require no-network repair and qualification before another live authorization request.

Adoption is prospective and migration-safe: historical D# records are not rewritten, and an active task may finish already authorized no-network implementation and QA but may not mint a new execution D# or live/spend authority under this proposed contract before its design and schema are separately approved.
